arxiv-2204-00723.title: Analysis of Sparse Subspace Clustering:
arxiv-2204-00723.creator: Experiments and Random Projection
arxiv-2204-00723.description: Abstract ABSTRACT Clustering can be defined as the process of assembling objects into a number of groups whose elements are similar to each other in some manner. As a technique that is used in many domains, such as face clustering, plant categorization, image segmentation, document classification, clustering is considered one of the most important unsupervised learning problems.

arxiv-2207-01604.title: Lower bounds for adiabatic quantum algorithms by quantum speed limits
arxiv-2207-01604.creator: Jyong-Hao Chen
arxiv-2207-01604.description: Abstract We introduce a simple framework for estimating lower bounds on the runtime of a broad class of adiabatic quantum algorithms. The central formula consists of calculating the variance of the final Hamiltonian with respect to the initial state. After examining adiabatic versions of certain keystone circuit-based quantum algorithms, this technique is applied to adiabatic quantum algorithms with undetermined speedup.

arxiv-2211-04967.title: Chromospheric activity and photospheric variation of α \alpha Ori during the great dimming event in 2020
arxiv-2211-04967.creator: M. Mittag, K.-P. Schröder, V. Perdelwitz, D. Jack, J.H.M.M. Schmitt
arxiv-2211-04967.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by M. Mittag, K.-P. Schröder, V. Perdelwitz, D. Jack, J.H.M.M. Schmitt. The so-called great dimming event of α \alpha Ori in late 2019 and early 2020 sparked our interest in the behaviour of chromospheric activity during this period. α \alpha Ori was already part of the long-term monitoring program of our TIGRE telescope to study the stellar activity of giant stars, and therefore regular measurements of α \alpha Ori have been taken since 2013.

arxiv-2306-13621.title: Ergodic properties of Brownian motion under stochastic resetting
arxiv-2306-13621.creator: E. Barkai 1 , R. Flaquer-Galmés 2 , V. Méndez 2
arxiv-2306-13621.description: Abstract We study ergodic properties of one-dimensional Brownian motion with resetting. Using generic classes of statistics of times between resets, we find respectively for thin/fat tailed distributions, the normalized/non-normalised invariant density of this process. The former case corresponds to known results in the resetting literature and the latter to infinite ergodic theory.

arxiv-2310-02367.title: Linear Recurrent Units for Sequential Recommendation CCS: Information systems Recommender systems
arxiv-2310-02367.creator: Zhenrui Yue, Yueqi Wang, Zhankui He, Huimin Zeng, Julian McAuley, Dong Wang
arxiv-2310-02367.description: Abstract . State-of-the-art sequential recommendation relies heavily on self-attention-based recommender models. Yet such models are computationally expensive and often too slow for real-time recommendation. Furthermore, the self-attention operation is performed at a sequence-level, thereby making low-cost incremental inference challenging. Inspired by recent advances in efficient language modeling, we propose l inear r ecurrent u nits for sequential rec ommenda-tion (LRURec).

arxiv-2511-06049.title: Phenomenology of the Minimal Scale Invariant Two-Higgs-Doublet Model
arxiv-2511-06049.creator: Nabil Baouche ID, Amine Ahriche ID
arxiv-2511-06049.description: Abstract We perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of the Scale Invariant Two Higgs Doublet Model ( SI2HDM ) Lee:2012jn . In this framework, the electroweak symmetry breaking is triggered radiatively, and the entire scalar mass spectrum, including that of the 125 125 GeV Higgs boson, is generated at the one loop level.

arxiv-2602-02594.title: Wilson loops as probes of phase transitions and conductivity phenomena
arxiv-2602-02594.creator: Tetiana Obikhod, Ievgenii Petrenko, [2mm] Institute for Nuclear Research NAS of Ukraine, Kyiv, Ukraine
arxiv-2602-02594.description: Abstract Wilson loops are among the most fundamental gauge-invariant observables in quantum field theory, encoding the global structure of gauge fields through their holonomy along closed contours. Originally introduced as order parameters for confinement in non-Abelian gauge theories, they have recently acquired a central role in condensed matter physics, where they characterize topological phases and quantized transport phenomena.

pmc-10651633.title: Physiologically based absorption modeling to predict the bioequivalence of two cilostazol formulations
pmc-10651633.creator: Lu Wang, Pengfei Zhao, Ting Luo, Dandan Yang, Qianqian Jiang, Jinliang Chen, Honggang Lou, Zourong Ruan, Bo Jiang
pmc-10651633.description: In vivo pharmacokinetic simulations and virtual bioequivalence (BE) evaluation of cilostazol have not yet been described for humans. Here, we successfully developed a physiologically based absorption model to simulate plasma concentrations of cilostazol. In addition, virtual population simulations integrating dissolution of 0.3% sodium dodecyl sulfate water media were executed to evaluate the BE of test and reference formulations.

pmc-10666020.creator: Luma Carolina Câmara Gradim, André Luiz Maciel Santana, Marcelo Archanjo José, Marcelo Knörich Zuffo, Roseli de Deus Lopes, Amaryllis Mavragani, Anand Mhatre, Cristina Turcu, Shahzad Ashraf, Athanasios Anastasiou

pmc-11332423.title: Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome Due to HIV Treatment as a Potential Trigger: A Case Report with Late-Onset Narcolepsy
pmc-11332423.creator: Jiaqin Yu, Ting Shen, Zongshan Li, Tian Lv, Lisan Zhang
pmc-11332423.description: Narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) is a unique central sleepiness disorder that affects individuals with excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS), cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic hallucinations. The etiology and pathogenesis of NT1 remains unclear, although some viral infections are thought to be related to NT1.

pmc-11710618.title: Neuronal mTORC1 is required for acute Aβ‐induced cognitive dysfunction
pmc-11710618.creator: Stacy A Hussong, Kylie M Williams, Veronica Galvan
pmc-11710618.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have found that mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activity is significantly increased in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) patients and mouse models of AD. Additionally, inhibition of mTORC1 with systemic rapamycin treatment ameliorates AD‐like phenotypes in several AD mouse models. However, the specific contribution of neuronal mTORC1 signaling in driving AD phenotypes has not yet been explored.

pmc-12557081.title: Evaluating Post-Earthquake Sexual and Reproductive Health Services in Türkiye: A Qualitative Study
pmc-12557081.creator: D Camur, AC Bilgin, O Turunc, BN Bugdaycı Yalcın, Z Kılınc, N Savas, T Inandı, B Kılıc
pmc-12557081.description: BackgroundMore than 50 thousand people lost their lives in the earthquake that occurred in Türkiye in 2023. This study aimed to evaluate the Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services provided in Hatay province with qualitative methods.MethodsThe research type is phenomenological. Purposeful and snowball sampling was conducted.

pmc-12819651.title: Data mining historical Chinese medical recipe collections and nuclear receptor profiling identify plant fractions that modulate glucocorticoid receptor activity
pmc-12819651.creator: Joachim Prackwieser, René Houtman, Tim Kievits, Diana Melchers, Haifeng Guan, Georg Seifert, Frank Konietschke, Kai Lamottke, Paul U. Unschuld, Nalini Kirk
pmc-12819651.description: ObjectiveGlucocorticoids (GCs) play a prominent role in the management of chronic inflammatory diseases like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis, but their use is associated with various adverse effects. The therapeutic and adverse effects of GCs can be partly explained by modes of engagement with their target, the glucocorticoid receptor (GR).

pmc-13262584.title: Lymphocyte-Predominant Ascites as a Clue to Peritoneal Tuberculosis: Two Case Reports and a Literature Review
pmc-13262584.creator: Wan Sun, Keyuan Lai, Chunxia Huang, Yuanyang Ye, Yuan Chen, Shaoqiang Xu
pmc-13262584.description: BackgroundPeritoneal tuberculosis (PTB) is difficult to diagnose because its clinical and imaging features are nonspecific and may mimic peritoneal malignancy or other intra-abdominal diseases. In addition, microbiological and molecular tests of ascitic fluid may be negative in paucibacillary disease.Case PresentationWe report two patients with PTB whose initial diagnostic evaluation was inconclusive.

pmc-13371701.title: APOE+ macrophages induce tumor cell metastatic characteristics via TNFSF12/TNFRSF12A signaling, correlating with poor patient prognosis
pmc-13371701.creator: Chuanjun Song, Hongyu Sun, Wenyuan Gan, Quanzhong Liu, Lingxiang Wu, Mengyan Zhu, Lingjun Zhu
pmc-13371701.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with metastasis representing a major determinant of poor prognosis. Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastatic progression by enhancing tumor cell migration and invasion. This study aimed to identify EMT-associated malignant epithelial programs in CRC and define the macrophage-tumor cell signaling mechanisms contributing to EMT and apoptosis resistance.

pmc-13651494.title: Precision gene editing technology to modulate genes in oral diseases: Therapeutic applications and delivery strategies
pmc-13651494.creator: Yihan Wang, Xuesong Li, Chunpeng Liu, Bing He, Yiming Liu, Qingyan Liu, Chenyu Liu, Daiyun Chen, Shufang Wang, Lin Zhang
pmc-13651494.description: Oral diseases represent a significant global health burden. Given the limited therapeutic efficacy of conventional mechanical interventions and antimicrobial treatments, there is a critical demand for targeted, precision therapies. Gene editing has emerged as a revolutionary approach that modifies specific genes to alter cellular phenotypes, leading to significant advances in human medicine.
